ArXiv cs.AI.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33161v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. Each has a known weakness: an answer can be fluent but insecure, mathematically plausible but physically infeasible, or rated highly by a judge while quietly breaking a task requirement. We propose a scoring framework that combines a small set of hard checks every answer must pass with a wider set of softer checks whose scores are blended into one number per candidate. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33303v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. ArXiv cs.AI.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Jacobian-Space: Language and Vision Models Agree Approximately Up to a Rotation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33304v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) posits that AI models converge toward a shared representation of the world, even when trained on different data modalities. Previous work has found evidence for the PRH in the activations of vision and language models. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A language model can name a brand without classifying it correctly. This study measures these outcomes separately for 1,000 B2B SaaS brands across 333 product categories. On Gemma 4 12B, with no external retrieval, category prompts elicit 510 brands (51.0%). A separate five-candidate category probe ranks the reference label first for 787 brands, a distractor first for 194, and yields little separation for 19. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33394v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. However, a single agentic task often combines easy and difficult subtasks, making one model choice for the entire task inefficient. We introduce partial routing, which guides a frontier lead model to delegate suitable subtasks to a cheaper worker model. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate low-level sensor observations that are not directly suitable for process analysis and must first be transformed into semantically meaningful events. This paper investigates collaborative language models as a zero-shot semantic abstraction layer for converting such observations into higher-level event and activity labels. ArXiv cs.AI.description:

ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33513v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents that operate in the real world must reason correctly and on-time, yet they currently do not account for how time should alter their reasoning. Modern agents learn to do tasks in environments that are entirely synchronous: where the world waits for the agent to act before changing. A real-time environment, by contrast, changes independent of the agent. Existing approaches try to bridge this gap by imposing a ratio of thinking to acting. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.33555v1 Announce Type: new
